title: The Burden of Freedom in Existential Thought
text:
A core tenet of existential philosophy posits that existence precedes essence. This means that humans are born into the world as blank slates, defining their own nature and meaning through lived experience and choice, rather than adhering to a predetermined blueprint or divine purpose.

This radical freedom, while empowering, simultaneously generates profound anxiety. The realization that one is entirely responsible for every action and inaction—and thus, responsible for creating not only oneself but also the image of humanity—is termed 'anguish.' This concept moves beyond simple moral responsibility; it speaks to the ontological weight of pure possibility.

Therefore, navigating existence requires confronting 'the nothing'—the void of inherent meaning. The objective is not merely self-actualization, but rather achieving authenticity by accepting this fundamental groundlessness and building value structures upon conscious commitment.
